notes: v242 — WORK-PROFILES (owner, Fri Oct 23, 2026 evening: "Build it tonight" — tomorrow Ai Trucking has no work and he drives one day for another carrier: different truck, different company charged, different rate, different tax, PTI on that truck, another ticket; his Ai Trucking / Truck 07 books stay untouched and separate). THE BUILD: (1) THE SEAM (js/app.js, App.workProfiles) — profiles persist as the work_profiles store key {list, activeId}; a profile carries company charged, truck number, licence plate, the rate its entries are paid at, rate-includes-tax + tax %, and its OWN next invoice number. The onboarding record stays the ACTIVE profile's working copy: switching folds the working copy into the profile being left and mirrors the incoming one in, so every existing reader (PTI pre-fill, invoice defaults, completion pricing) follows the active profile with no second source of truth. MIGRATION: while the key is absent, Profile 1 is DERIVED from the account's existing settings on every read (his: AI Trucking, Truck 07, plate 04 R209, $29, tax-included @5%, next invoice 1152); the first mutation persists it verbatim, and every unstamped legacy record reads as Profile 1. (2) PREFERENCES gains the WORK PROFILES card (driver/both faces; office-only accounts never drive and don't get it, like the Truck card): the profile list with the active one marked, one-tap Use this profile (a switch first flushes the profile-owned form fields exactly as they stand), Add profile, and an in-card editor for the seven fields. A Preferences Save also captures the profile-owned facts onto the active profile's record. (3) STAMPING — every new record carries the active profileId: PTI reports (the form pre-fills carrier/unit/plate from the ACTIVE profile and names it on a Working-for line; the v241 plate write-back now lands on the active profile), dispatches (stamped at creation; a completion prices at the RECORD's own profile rate and posts its revenue entry into that book), revenue entries + extras, tracker sessions (stamped at session START — manual and auto-start — so a running session keeps its starting profile through a mid-day switch; the close review prices at the session's rate and names its book), and manifests (a day prices at the rate of the profile its own stamped records name). (4) BOOKS PER PROFILE — Revenue reads scope to the active profile (day totals, month, chart, glance); writers work on the full lists and translate scoped indices, so a save can never drop the other profile's records; the v241 one-close law is judged inside the session's own book (a completion under one profile never eats the other's tracker entry, and a late re-stop converges in the book it started in). The Invoice module shows/aggregates ONLY the active profile's entries: issued list, open period, revenue plan (per-profile rate), per-profile drafts (inv_drafts; the legacy inv_draft remains Profile 1's), scoped numbering + collisions inside invIssue/invCycMarkSettled/invCycRemoveSettled (no profile named = the pre-v242 whole-book behaviour, byte for byte), and the stored period inputs are stamped with their book (papid) so one book's period never opens in the other. (5) VISIBILITY — the dashboard tracker card names the active profile on a quiet chip (company + truck, painted by trackerPaint); the PTI form and the close-day review name the book the day lands in. (6) SYNC — profiles sync as a settings key; stamps ride inside records, and the v241 record-union keeps the stamped copy (it is the more complete copy) — proven in the harness. Connect behaviour untouched; P&L's unscoped plan door unchanged. REPRODUCTION-FIRST: tools/work-profiles-v242-test.js — written first, RED on the shipped v241 code (no seam), now 90/90: migration invariance with his real October figures (Oct 16-31 plan $1,798.00 before AND after; Oct 22's single $319.00 entry; glance unchanged), cross-profile isolation (invoice plan / month totals / glance), PTI plates per profile on the real module, mid-day switch semantics, independent numbering (#1152->#1153 for Ai; the new profile starts at its own #1; #1152 is free inside the other book), seam round-trips, and union stamp survival. REGRESSIONS: full 166-suite sweep — fail set identical to the pre-change measured baseline (background-day 3, chart-legibility-v151 5 [calendar-frozen], chatbot 2, connect-pipe 76/77 parked pin, dispatch-autostart 1 [wall-clock], fix-batch-v222 1, loads-gps-fix-v203 crash, native-track 1, navigator 178/180 parked stub, navigator-v139 2, navigator-screen 1, gesture-plane 6, gestures 5, boss-firstrun 142/144, pti-dash 1, role-package 174/177 — all pre-existing) plus the new suite green; the ?v=241 index cohort and the standing ship pins move 241 -> 242. Native unchanged (v42 shell + iPhone web pick it up). THE SAME-NIGHT TRAP PASS (prepared spec, Oct 23 ~18:32 — the one-day temp-truck traps): (T1) THE ODOMETER IS PER TRUCK — the master, the dated readings log, the annual-sticker date, the service-sticker targets, the service book and the sticker photos all live in the ACTIVE profile's chain: Profile 1 keeps the legacy keys (mt_odo / odo_readings / mt_annualDate / mt_*) byte-for-byte, any other profile gets its own '__<pid>' keys, so a temp truck's lower dash can never drag Truck 07's master down, poison its lifetime km or move its PM countdowns — and its own readings start their own chain from its first photo. The core chain functions (masterOdometer / bumpOdometer / logOdoReading / seed / import / odoMasterNow) resolve the chain key inline from the seam; the seed only ever takes evidence stamped with the chain's own profile (service events seed Profile 1 only); a dispatch-close stamp reads the SESSION's own truck's log even if the day closes after a switch; the safety-sticker expiry and the odometer-baseline draft are CARRIED on the profile record (they move with the truck; they are not editor fields). Fuel fills are stamped with their profile at creation. (T2) THE CONNECT FENCE — a day carrying ANY non-Profile-1 stamp (dispatch, session or revenue entry) never publishes: publishDay refuses it, the records doc filters temp fills and temp PTI reports out, billing never carries a temp profile's invoice, and manifest days for fenced dates contribute no lines to any peer's doc. Ai Trucking connections see Ai days only. (The shared maintenance facts still read Truck 07's physical keys on purpose: that doc IS Truck 07's book.) (T3) SWITCH-BACK IS EXACT — proven in the harness: A→B→A restores the working copy byte-for-byte (company, truck, plate, rate, tax, next invoice #1152) and Profile 1's stored record and October plan ($1,798.00) are bit-identical after the round trip. (T4) SWITCH-BACK PROMPT — the close review under a non-main profile carries one quiet secondary button, 'End shift & switch back to Ai Trucking · Truck 07': it runs the ordinary Confirm first (the close lands whole in the day's own book, the end-odometer in its own truck's chain) and only then switches. (T5) START TIME — the autostart plan never looks at profiles: the temp dispatch's scheduled time drives the session start exactly as an Ai dispatch's does, the 8:00 AM Mon–Sat rule stays the fallback, and the session is stamped with the temp profile at its start. HARNESS: tools/work-profiles-v242-test.js is now 132/132 — sections (i) odometer isolation + seed fence + sticker carry, (j) the Connect fence (real CP._dayFenced over stamped fixtures + wiring pins), (k) byte-exact switch-back, (l) close-prompt + start-time pins join (a)–(h).
